tagline: Along the Divide to the valley where Sacajawea was born.
intro: From Interstate 15 the byway takes Idaho 33 west past Terreton and Mud Lake, then Idaho 28 northwest, a mostly straight road that runs beside the Continental Divide for almost 100 miles. It crosses Gilmore Summit, a low pass at 7,186 feet, and follows the Lemhi River down the Lemhi Valley to Salmon.

The valley is the homeland of the Lemhi Shoshone, the Agaidika or salmon eaters, and Sacajawea was born here. She came back in 1805 with the Corps of Discovery and interpreted when they bargained with her people for horses and a guide.
season: Visit Idaho says year-round: summer is the easier travel, and autumn color is best from late September through October.

moments.title: Birch Creek Charcoal Kilns
moments.text: Sixteen beehive kilns, each about 20 feet tall, made charcoal here for the Nicholia smelter for less than three years, and four of them still stand.

moments.title: Leadore
moments.text: Leadore grew up in 1910 around the repair shops of the Gilmore and Pittsburgh Railroad, which quit in 1939, and a replica of its depot now serves as the community center.

moments.title: Salmon
moments.text: The Sacajawea center in Salmon tells her story along a trail past a tipi camp, a riverside sweat lodge and a fish weir.
